subject: Post-demo alignment: TPS signal, monthly burn range, and next steps
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Sep 2029 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo alignment: TPS signal, monthly burn range, and next steps

Hi Samir — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the specific asks we promised to get aligned on so procurement has what they need: 

- Consumption shape (what you told us):
  • Pilot / Q4: ~50M tokens / month
  • Post-rollout (Q1 onward): steady-state 100–120M tokens / month
  • Short burst windows: expected peaks of ~110–130 QPS for 90–120s during business hours (user-driven).

- Budget target / unit economics you mentioned on the call: target ~$30 / 1M tokens as a blended number across generation + embeddings.

What we need from you to finalize a hosted quote and SOW draft:
1) Confirm the monthly expectation bracket (50M baseline vs. 100–120M steady-state). If there are multiple consumer tiers with different token mix (e.g., embeddings-heavy vs. generation-heavy), a rough split helps.
2) Confirm the expected peak TPS (you said ~120 QPS peak; is the 110–130 range accurate?).
3) Any procurement timelines or budget approval windows we should be aware of (Doc sign date target).

Attached is an updated price spreadsheet (redwood_price_estimate_v2.xlsx) that sketches three pricing bands (pilot, growth, steady-state) and the estimated $/1M token at each band, plus optional burst protection for sustained 99th-percentile QPS.

Next steps I propose: if you confirm the numbers above, we’ll:
- Lock a hosted pricing range and send a short SOW draft for procurement review (1–2 business days).
- Have our SE (Karthik) join a 30-min throughput validation session to walk through the expected 99th % latency and throttling behavior.

Available times for the SE session: Thu 9/12 10:30–11:00 PT or Fri 9/13 14:00–14:30 PT. Let me know what works.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi

Subject: Re: Post-demo alignment: TPS signal, monthly burn range, and next steps

Thanks Irene — appreciate the clear summary. Confirming the numbers from our side: 

- Monthly token expectation: pilot in Q4 ~50M tokens / month. Production long-run expected to be 100–120M tokens / month within 10–12 weeks after rollout. The mix is roughly 70% generation, 30% embeddings initially; embeddings may grow over time.
- Peak TPS: our internal telemetry shows occasional spikes up to ~120 QPS, sometimes short bursts to 140 QPS but usually for <30 seconds. For planning, use 130 QPS as a conservative peak.
- Budget target: procurement is targeting $28–32 / 1M tokens; $30 / 1M is the sweet spot they’d like to see.

Procurement timeline: Procurement will review SOW next Wed (9/18). If we can get a draft by EOW (9/13) that would be ideal.

Let me know if you need any traffic profile exports from our side (I can ask infra to share a 7-day qps histogram).

—Samir

Thanks for looping us in — copying the customer for context. Replied inline to Samir's numbers below and spelled out recommended scenarios for the hosted quote spreadsheet: 

> Samir: monthly 50M -> 100–120M, peaks ~130 QPS, target ~$30 / 1M

Our notes / recommendation: 
- Pricing bands: Pilot (0–60M), Growth (60–120M), Steady (120M+). The blended $/1M at the $30 target only holds if we assume a modest 10–15% KV-cache and batching efficiencies. If their generation:embedding mix shifts to more embeddings, unit costs decrease (embeddings tokens cheaper to serve).
- Peak protection: Since their conservative peak is 130 QPS with occasional 140 QPS <30s, I recommend we include a short-burst buffer (automatic burst allowance up to +25% QPS for 2 minutes) and a sustained-surge plan for >5m windows that would trigger autoscale (and clear pricing view).
- Hosted vs Dedicated note: If the true 99th percentile sustained QPS exceeds ~100 QPS for extended windows (multi-minute), Dedicated or Reserved capacity can materially reduce unit cost. Recommend we model both hosted (with burst protection) and a dedicated seat price in the spreadsheet for procurement to compare.

Action items: 
1) Irene — can you confirm Samir is OK with the 9/13 EOW SOW target? If yes I’ll produce a second tab in the spreadsheet with a Dedicated SKU comparison.
2) Marissa — can you shepherd the SOW/SLA language once the numbers are locked so procurement has the SLA and data-handling clauses they require?
3) Samir — if you can share the 7-day qps histogram that will let us refine the 99th% and pricing band inputs.

Happy to jump on the SE session Thu 9/12 10:30PT if that slot still works — I can bring the throughput runbook.

Cheers,
Karthik
